summary: Let mvmAI act on your own data in your other installed apps.

features.title: Personal data bridge
features.short: Point a chat at one of your apps and let mvmAI read or change your data there
features.description: Choose one of your apps in the chat, such as Budget or Calendar, and mvmAI can look things up and add or change things in it, but only for your own account. The list holds the apps you added to your Apps Hub profile whose app-to-app API the administrator enabled, and it picks up any new action an app adds. Every change is first shown as a form with the values mvmAI filled in, where you can correct them and save or cancel, and mvmAI reports only what was actually saved. It can never see or touch another user's data. Without a subscription the app picker is shown locked on the desktop and the assistant answers with a plain chat only. Several independent changes are reviewed as pages of one form; correct or exclude any entry before saving the selected changes together. Functions marked internal by an app are never offered to the assistant.

features.title: Public page AI
features.short: Use a different AI provider and model for the public page
features.description: mvmAI's public page can talk to a different provider and model than the desktop app — for example, a cheaper or faster model for anonymous visitors while the desktop keeps a stronger one for the administrator. Without a subscription the public page always uses the same provider and model configured for the desktop.

features.title: Adjustable chat history
features.short: Choose how many recent messages stay in full before mvmAI summarizes
features.description: mvmAI keeps a chat's most recent messages in full and folds everything older into a running summary, so long conversations don't grow more expensive per reply forever. With a subscription the administrator can raise or lower how many recent messages stay in full, on both the desktop app and the public page. Without a subscription this is fixed at 20 messages.

features.title: Terminal next to the chat
features.short: A real terminal beside the chat, started with your AI tool and kept running
features.description: With the setting turned on, the mvmAI window on the desktop gets a terminal button. The terminal opens over the chat, at the bottom or on the right, and starts the command-line tool of the chat's provider, such as Claude, Codex or Gemini, so you can type that tool's own commands, like /usage, yourself. It hides when you click anywhere else. The pin button keeps it docked beside the chat and open every time you return to that chat, while a new chat starts without one. Its session keeps running while it is hidden or the window is closed, so the tool does not ask about trusting the folder every time; the close button ends it. This works only on the desktop. Without a subscription the setting is shown locked and the button opens the Premium dialog.
